opening_message:
Ticket 1: Miguel Benson (employee ID E006) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E006.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer and requests admin access to Source Code. Since Engineers own the Source Code system, admin is permitted for full-time employees under policy. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E006 (Miguel Benson) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Requested admin exceeds the maximum; recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type. Note 1 (HR) claims E006 is full-time and recommends admin; Note 2 (Security) claims it looked up E006 in its own database and found he is a contractor with basic security training, explicitly stating he is "not full-time." Contractors may never have admin; with only basic training the maximum is read. Because the requested level (admin) exceeds the contractor maximum, and the security record directly contradicts the HR employment claim, I grant the maximum allowed: read.
